business.description: ODigMa Consultancy Solutions Limited is a full-service digital marketing company founded in 2010, offering services across web development, email marketing, social media, programmatic advertising, video production, SEO, AEO, and GEO. The company serves 150+ clients across India with a team of 120+ professionals across 10+ cities.

outlook.statement: India's advertising expenditure projected to reach ₹1,476 billion (USD 15.9 billion) by 2026; digital advertising forecast to reach ₹69,856 crore by 2026 (61% of total ad spend). Shift toward AI-first discovery (GEO, LLM-led answers, AI agents running marketing workflows) and DPDP Act forcing brands to rethink targeting/measurement. Vernacular/regional content opportunity: 73% of internet subscribers consume regional content, 540 million users, ₹4.5 lakh crore market. Influencer marketing projected ~USD 400 million in India in 2026, growing ~25% annually. Quick commerce emerging as standalone discovery/performance channel (Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart). Purpose-driven/sustainability-led marketing gaining traction with under-35 consumers.

The Company expects that the benefits of this transition, including reduced reliance on external contractors and improved operational efficiencies, will support profitability over the medium to long term.

risks: Rapid Technological Disruption: AI reshaping search, content, campaign management; service methodologies can become outdated quickly; pressure to master AEO/GEO alongside traditional SEO

Rising Media Costs and Talent Pressure: CPMs on Meta and Google risen significantly, squeezing margins; retaining skilled professionals in data analytics, AI-driven content, performance marketing remains challenging
Client Concentration Risk: Dependence on limited high-value clients or specific verticals exposes agency to revenue volatility during sector downturns or client budget shifts
The Board is of the opinion that there are no risks which, in its opinion, may threaten the existence of the Company.
The Company manages foreign exchange risk and hedges to the extent considered necessary as and when required.
Actuarial risk: Adverse Salary Growth Experience, Variability in mortality rates, Variability in withdrawal rates
Investment risk: For funded plans relying on insurers, asset values may not reflect fair value, causing fluctuations in net liability
Liquidity risk: High-salary/long-duration employees resigning/retiring can strain cashflows
Market risk: Discount rate fluctuations (linked to corporate/government bond yields) materially affect defined benefit obligation valuation
Legislative risk: Amendments to Payment of Gratuity Act could increase plan liabilities
Credit risk: Trade receivables are typically unsecured; maximum exposure Rs 686.98 crore (2026), Rs 864.79 crore (2025)
Liquidity risk: Company monitors liquidity position and deploys robust cash management system
Market risk: Exposure to foreign currency risk (primarily USD); no derivative hedging used
Foreign currency sensitivity: +5% USD rate increases profit before tax by Rs 31.30 crore (2026), Rs 12.56 crore (2025)
